parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReceivingService is an application/domain service. It coordinates stock operations: it looks up an item and a bin, then calls the domain behaviour (Bin.put, Bin.take, Item.needsReorder). It also applies a business policy in pick(), filling the request greedily across the bins that hold the SKU and then deciding whether to reorder. Saving and loading are delegated to the injected tables through find, holding and store, so the file has no SQL, connection handling, transport or framework code. The only persistence-flavoured part is a thin step that turns row objects into Bin/Item through their constructors and spreads ({ ...bin }) when storing. That is a minor mapping concern, not a misplaced persistence responsibility. The constructor depends on concrete persistence table classes, but that is a question of import and dependency direction, which this rule excludes. No business rules or other responsibilities from another layer kind were found.
